title: Oto-Manguean languages - Wikipedia
text: Oto-Manguean is widely viewed as a proven language family. The highest number of speakers of Oto-Manguean languages today is in the Mexican state of Oaxaca, where the two largest branches, the Zapotecan and the Mixtecan languages, are spoken by almost 1.5 million people combined.

title: Mixtec, Yosondúa Language (MPM) – L1 & L2 Speakers, Status ...
text: Yosondúa Mixtec is an endangered indigenous language of Mexico. It belongs to the Otomanguean language family. The language is used as a first language by all adults in the ethnic community, but not all young people. It is not known to be taught in schools.

text: Mar 21, 2025 · Yosondúa Mixtec, spoken by around 6,000 people in Oaxaca, Mexico, is part of the Mixtec branch of the Oto-Manguean family. It holds cultural importance among the Yosondúa people.
